title: The Last Provision
premise: Salvage diver Marguerite Okafor is hired to quietly recover a wreck on a border river the navy pretends not to see, and she intends to stay as invisible as she has for three years since the accident that killed her dive partner. When her team raises a sealed chest stamped with the crest of a nation that no longer exists, she realizes the wreck was a courier boat carrying evidence of a massacre the surviving government will do anything to bury. Hunted by a naval officer who once loved her and a fixer she cannot trust, Marguerite must ferry the chest—and her makeshift crew of misfits—downriver to a journalist in the delta. In the end she chooses truth over silence, losing her anonymity and nearly her life, but gaining a family bound by what they carried together.
about_author: Paloma Marchetti is a former maritime archaeologist who spent a decade documenting river wrecks across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes from a houseboat on the Danube, where her neighbors still suspect she is hiding from something.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She dives a routine salvage job, establishing her rule of invisibility and the ritual by which she counts her life in river miles since her partner Tomas died. A navy liaison offers her a lucrative, off-the-books contract on a restricted stretch of river. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: The Navy's Silence
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She assembles her crew—engineer Bo, cook-diver Ines, and teenage deckhand Kofi—and signs the contract with its suspicious secrecy clauses. First survey of the wreck site reveals the hull was holed from the inside. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional confidence.

chapters.title: Cold Water, Old Bones
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The first dive finds human remains chained in the cargo hold, and Ines, who carries her own war scars, insists they stop. Marguerite overrides her, needing the money. Emotional beat: the first fracture in the crew's trust.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Deep in the flooded hold, Marguerite pries loose a lead-lined chest bearing the seal of Veltania, a state erased from maps twenty years ago. She hides it from the navy liaison. Emotional beat: the moment invisibility becomes impossible.

chapters.title: Officer Reyes
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The naval officer overseeing the contract is revealed to be Marguerite's former lover, who believes she drowned three years ago. He suspects the chest has been moved and struggles between duty and old feeling. Emotional beat: love sharpened into surveillance.

chapters.title: A Chest of Paper Bones
chapters.summary: Kofi's POV. The crew secretly opens the chest: manifests, photographs, and orders documenting the Veltanian deportations. Kofi, an orphan of that same conflict, recognizes a camp in the photos. Emotional beat: history becoming personal.

chapters.title: The Fixer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A charming broker named Sable appears at a riverport offering to buy the chest outright and hinting he knows what she carries. Marguerite pretends ignorance but realizes the secret is already leaking. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Night Run
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. To avoid a navy checkpoint, they run the rapids at night without lights. Bo's engineering holds, barely, and the near-death bonds the crew into something like family. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into loyalty.

chapters.title: The Price of Quiet
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines confronts Marguerite: keeping the chest means painting a target on Kofi and everyone aboard. Marguerite confesses about Tomas and the accident she caused. Emotional beat: guilt finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes intercepts Sable and learns the chest's contents—and that his own government signed the orders inside. Ordered to recover it at any cost, he requests one concession: Marguerite comes in alive. Emotional beat: duty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Stowaway's Story
chapters.summary: Kofi's POV. Kofi tells the crew how he survived the camps and why the documents matter to the living, not the dead. The vote is unanimous: take the chest to the delta journalist, Ade Balogun, whom Ines trusts. Emotional beat: found family forged by shared purpose.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A patrol boat burns a fishing village that sheltered them overnight. Marguerite realizes the navy will kill civilians to bury the chest. Emotional beat: rage replacing caution.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable corners Marguerite alone, revealing he represents a Veltanian exile council willing to pay a fortune—or expose her to Reyes if she refuses. She stalls, buying time but owing a debt. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Locks
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. At the canal locks, Bo discovers Ines has been radioing coordinates—to Balogun, she claims, but the navy arrives minutes later. The crew scatters into the marshes with the chest. Emotional beat: trust shattered at the worst moment.

chapters.title: The Marsh Cathedral
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Hiding in a flooded church, Marguerite and Kofi wait out the search while Ines proves her innocence—she was feeding Balogun a decoy route. Reyes finds them alone and, seeing the photographs, wavers. Emotional beat: mercy inside the hunt.

chapters.title: What Reyes Carries
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes lets them go but cannot come with them; instead he gives Marguerite the patrol schedule and a stolen radio, knowing it ends his career. Emotional beat: love choosing truth over duty.

chapters.title: The Delta Gate
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The final run to the delta: Sable's boat blocks the channel, and Reyes's navy closes from behind. Marguerite rams the blockade, taking damage that leaves them dead in the water two miles from Balogun's safehouse. Emotional beat: all-or-nothing desperation.

chapters.title: Two Miles of Water
chapters.summary: Kofi's POV. With the engine dead, the crew swims and paddles the chest through crocodile water by night, Kofi's childhood water skills saving them. Bo is wounded covering their escape from Sable's men. Emotional beat: the crew becoming one body, one breath.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They reach Balogun, but Sable holds Bo and demands the chest. Marguerite offers herself and the documents' location, gambling that Balogun has already transmitted scans abroad. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy, love as leverage.

chapters.title: The Story Goes Out
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Balogun's story breaks worldwide while Sable's leverage evaporates; Bo is freed, and Sable, exposed as a double agent for the old regime, is arrested. The massacre has a name again. Emotional beat: catharsis—the dead given back their voices.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the inquiry, Marguerite testifies publicly for the first time in three years, naming Tomas and her own fault in his death. Reyes, stripped of command, chooses to stay near her anyway. Emotional beat: accountability as the beginning of forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Next Mile
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue. The crew refits the boat under a new contract: mapping the river's lost wrecks openly, for the historical record. Marguerite still counts miles, but now they are miles she chooses, with people who chose her back. Emotional beat: survival transformed into home.
